newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says to release corn/barley from grain stock.
newsitem.headline: Japan says to release corn/barley from grain stock.

text.p: Japan's Agriculture Ministry said on Friday it would release up to 400,000 tonnes of corn and up to 300,000 tonnes of barley from national feed grain stocks in the September/November period of this year.

The decisions were due to expected delayed shipments of corn and barley during the period, mainly from the United States, because of historically low grain stock levels there, a senior official of the Agriculture Ministry said.

"Delayed grain shipments are expected from the U.S. before the new crop arrives. We decided to release the feed grain stocks to secure stable feed supplies for farmers," said Mitsuhiro Yokoyama of the ministry's Livestock Industry Bureau.
The Japanese government began stockpiling feed grain in 1976, following shortages in the early 1970s in key producing countries such as the United States.
The Agriculture Ministry currently has 800,000 tonnes of corn and 400,000 tonnes of barley stockpiled.
